CPKC Distributed Power Placement Instructions 1 05.15.26 
Distributed Power Placment Instructions 
General Rules 
• Unless otherwise exempted in the chart below, train builds must comply with the 
GOI/ABTH. 
• All trains are restricted to maximum of three remote consists. 
• Maximum DP train length is 14,000 feet unless otherwise authorized. 
o Southern Regions maximum train length – 12,000 feet. 
• Mixed trains may not operate in excess of 25,000 tons without prior authorization. 
o Superintendent (or higher) must submit a request to 
DL_Simulation_Request@cpkcr.com at least 24 hours prior to intended train 
operation.   
o Requests must include: 
▪ Train symbol, origin, destination, and planned route;  
▪ Planned consist information, including locomotive configuration and online 
work events; and 
▪ A contact name and telephone number. 
 
GOI/ABTH Permitted Train Builds 
On all trains, equivalent driving axles are restricted to any combination of the following: 
• Lead consist – 24 (2 locomotives). 
• In-train remote consist(s) – 12 (1 Locomotive). 
• Rear remote consist – 12 (1 Locomotive). 
Note: 2-0-1 and 1-0-1 configurations are not permitted on the Haverty subdivision. 
 
Mid-Train Remote Placement Requirements 
On all bulk trains: 
• A single mid-train remote must be placed within +/- 5 cars of the train length mid-
point. 
• Multiple-remote trains must have remotes placed at equal distances (balanced) 
within the train to distribute in-train forces, within +/- 5 cars. 
On all mixed trains: 
• A single mid-train remote must be placed within +/- 1000 feet of the train length 
mid-point (excluding 201 and 401). 
• Multiple-remote trains should have remotes placed at equal distances (balanced) 
within the train to distribute in-train forces and must not exceed 1,000 feet of 
difference between DP sections. 
 
 
Every train configuration must pass TrAM prior to operating in any TrAM area. 
 
*This does not apply to the US Southern Region where MCS is the primary train 
build tool in use.

sections.text:
CPKC Distributed Power Placement Instructions 2 05.15.26 
 
 
Footnotes 
ALL This foot note applies to all distributed power trains:  Unless otherwise specified, all trains are 
permitted to operate with any combination of distributed power locomotives, provided the chosen 
configuration does not exceed 2 locomotives in the lead consist, 1 locomotive in the mid-train 
position, and 1 locomotive at the rear of the train. Examples: 2-1-1, 2-1-0, 2-0-1, 1-1-1, 1-0-1, 1-1-0.   
▲ Eastward Intermodal trains assembled at VIF may exceed the 1,000-foot placement rule if lifting 
enroute on the Cascade Sub, to bring length to design, and may include up to 3,750 feet of autoracks 
behind the lead locomotive consist. 
1  Applies to a maximum of 2,460 tons per locomotive, to a maximum of 139 cars. 
2  Reserved. 
3  Applies to 170 car trains (winter), and up to 205 cars (summer): Bredenbury/Broadview – Regina – 
Calgary – Vancouver route only.  2-2-1, 2-1-1, 1-2-1, 2-0-2 authorized Geddis to Vancouver only. 
4  Applies to 170 car trains Bredenbury/Broadview – Calgary – Vancouver route only.  2-0-2 authorized 
Geddis to Vancouver only.   
5  Authorized on Belle Plaine Subdivision subject to tractive effort restrictions identified in Timetable 
instructions. 
6  Loaded grain trains 1-1-1 prohibited on Laggan and Mountain Subs. 
7  Summer only account brake pipe gradient in colder temperatures. 
8  Applies to sand trains only. 
9 In this configuration, a train length of up to 16,000 feet is authorized between Deltaport and Mile 70 
Cascade Sub only. 
10 Applicable between Minnedosa and Winnipeg only. The two tail-end remote locomotives must be 
SD70-type.

Footnotes 
ALL This foot note applies to all distributed power trains:  Unless otherwise specified, all trains are 
permitted to operate with any combination of distributed power locomotives, provided the chosen

position, and 1 locomotive at the rear of the train. Examples: 2-1-1, 2-1-0, 2-0-1, 1-1-1, 1-0-1, 1-1-0.  
Exception: 2-0-1 and 1-0-1 configurations are not permitted on the Haverty subdivision 
1  Applies to a maximum of 2,460 tons per locomotive, to a maximum of 139 cars.

3  Summer only account brake pipe gradient in colder temperatures. 
4  Applies to sand trains only. 
5 Applicable on the US Southern Region only between Kansas City and Laredo. No empty cars are

6 Applicable to crude oil trains operating with up to 90 cars on the US Southern Region between

7 Applicable to 100 car grain trains operating from Pittsburg to Wade.
